profile_text.body:
Thinking Machines Lab is a for-profit artificial intelligence research and product startup founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, California. On its own site the company describes itself as building a future where everyone has access to the knowledge and tools to make AI work for their needs and goals, and says it aims to make AI systems more widely understood, customizable and generally capable. It states that it plans to publish technical blog posts, papers and code frequently, and that it favors multimodal systems built for human-AI collaboration over fully autonomous systems, along with model intelligence at the frontier in domains such as science and programming.

The company describes its team as scientists, engineers and builders who have worked on AI products and projects including ChatGPT, Character.ai, Mistral, PyTorch, OpenAI Gym, Fairseq and Segment Anything. It outlines an empirical and iterative approach to AI safety, listing three intended contributions: maintaining a high safety bar while maximizing user freedom, sharing best practices and recipes for building safe systems with the industry, and accelerating external research on alignment by sharing code, datasets and model specs. It also cites red-teaming and post-deployment monitoring as methods developed for present-day systems that it expects to extend to more capable ones.

The record shows no lawsuits against the company, and its legal exposure is listed in California.
